definition: The practice of splitting documents into retrieval units based on semantic coherence (like topic or section boundaries) rather than a fixed number of characters or tokens.
details: Semantic chunking aims to improve retrieval-augmented generation quality by keeping semantically related content together in the same chunk, rather than arbitrarily cutting sentences or ideas in half.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Semantic Chunking — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
